summary: The first screen mismatch remains the step-1763 rehumanization urgency defect in polyself.c polyman/rehumanize, with a tested worker correction queued for integration. The complete monster-spell dispatcher and four return-valued clerical helpers now have matching production recordings. The later RNG divergence at step1784 is source-located in wizard.c nasty, which is still missing with mcast_summon_mons; the minion.msummon dependency is under implementation. The aligned/high-cleric creation fallback remains a separate gap.
evidence: Checkpoint cf362473 matches 1782/1814 Knight screens, 1784/1814 cursors and 106855/108275 RNG values. The fixed workload matches 11364/11405 screens and all 404 recordings pass; compared with 2e2c6c14, no session loses a screen match, Knight gains 18 RNG values and one cursor match. Knight has 32 actual unmatched screens; the queue upper bound is 51.

The refreshed A42 scan still places the first screen and cursor difference at step1763, Escape input: C shows You return to human form! You can see again.--More-- with cursor [53,0,1], while JS retains the psi-bolt line with cursor [66,17,1]. The first cell difference is row0, column3. The later first RNG difference is at step1784, index106852: C nasty(wizard.c:607) calls rn2(10)=5, while JS calls rn2(5)=0 after skipping the still-unported summoning effect.

The source psi-bolt damage roll d(12,6)=34 produces the same human form in both implementations. C polyself.c polyman calls urgent_pline, but JS polyman prefers rawEnv.message; rehumanize supplies the ordinary message operation even though the monster-attack environment has a separate urgentMessage operation. A bounded corrected replay (run-nktyXU) shows recorded step1763 with You return to human form! You can see again.--More-- and cursor [53,0,1], and reaches the later effect17 boundary. Its diagnostic hook i1764 corresponds to recorded step1763. The corrected code has not yet passed main’s combined checkpoint.

The former mcast_spell effect17 refusal is removed by the complete dispatcher, which records the discarded mcast_summon_mons call as unported. The scan now emits1788 screens and later stops at an unsupported blocked-path hero-move message; that stop follows the known missing nasty RNG/state effects and does not establish an independent movement defect.

Four independent Grand Master recordings now complete lightning, paralysis, geyser and fire-pillar effects through castmu/mcast_spell and mdamageu: 375 screens and12696 RNG calls match. The dispatcher source span is closed, while the goal remains parked with void-effect families explicitly open. The failed earlier checkpoint had only a stale covetous-planning refusal test; the corrected test verifies tactics recomputes clone strategy/goal while live retries stay unchanged.

The read.c create_particular_creation affirmative response is now compared with numeric byte 121, matching cmd.js y_n and restoring the original species after cant_revive. The source-pinned affirmative production test passes; an independent negative-response recording matches 46 screens/cursors and 3185 RNG calls. The affirmative recording is blocked next in makemon.c priest/minion initialization and is retained as a recipe, not completion evidence.

Resolved step 1761: C finishes the casting announcement and effect message before damage. Awaiting the async JS messages and result-valued helpers moves the first difference to 1763 without changing RNG. Independent master-lich recording lich-spell-order-variation matches 2378 RNG calls and 57 screens/cursors; it does not establish clerical effect coverage.

Whole mhitu.c getmattk now handles seduction, disease/hunger, energy, temporary holder, weapon, cold-touch and home-elemental substitutions through mattacku/mattackm. Source-pinned tests establish the pure helper; unported uhitm.c hmonas remains a separate caller gap.

Retained counter-evidence: the earlier cleric fire-trap event had exactly one m_move→postmov→mintrap chain. Cleric2321 lacked minion state and trap knowledge because createMonsterBody skipped mk_roamer. A prior fire trap belonged to actor2334 at(26,7), outside learning range; fire resistance cannot omit the initial C fire-damage draw. The corrected source initialization removes that earlier divergence.

Retained counter-evidence for the resolved step1742 issue: the bat had spent its movement ration; its two distfleeck calls described one action. Vampire shapechange does not apply the Hell-bat creation-speed adjustment.

source.branch: C polyman uses urgent_pline for the restored-form announcement. JS selects an ordinary callback passed through rehumanize, which preserves WIN_STOP and suppresses the source urgent output. The queued correction preserves urgentMessage and planning silence, clears WIN_STOP after vision/map flush as C tty_putstr does, and follows redotoplin home/putsyms/cl_end without pre-clearing recorder shadow cells.

JS mattacku/castmu/mcast_spell propagate message and urgentMessage through mdamageu and rehumanize; polyman currently chooses the ordinary message callback for the source urgent announcement.
dependencies: The create_particular_creation response-byte defect is fixed. Ordinary aligned/high-cleric creation still lacks makemon.c fallback minion allocation and its rn2(3), renegade/peacefulness and set_malign sequence; its affirmative recipe remains blocked. Grand Master creation avoids that unrelated source branch and now has four complete clerical-effect recordings.

The complete mcast_spell dispatcher and all four return-valued clerical effects are implemented and recorded. Its discarded void mcast_summon_mons call remains a named gap. The current later RNG divergence is wizard.c nasty at step1784; worker A implements mcast_summon_mons/nasty, while worker B implements its return-valued minion.c msummon dependency and the runtime creation support required by that caller.
